RESOLUTION #9-26: Mr. Brenneman advised of the proposed Resolution declaring the 2019

Amended and Restated Little Britain Township Zoning Ordinance substantively invalid insofar as it

excludes data centers and ancillary buildings or uses, including but not limited to energy generating

facilities. The proposed Resolution is to allow the township to begin a curative amendment process as

authorized by section 609.2 of the Municipal Planning Code. Following a review of this information,

the meeting was open for public comment, with no response. A motion was then made by Mr. Beiler,

seconded by Mr. Coates and carried to adopt Resolution #9-26.

The county's Planning & Community Development Department, working with consultant Entech Engineering, introduced a full draft curative amendment (covering power sourcing, water supply, permitted zones, setbacks, noise, and decommissioning) to the County Planning Commission in September 2026; Commission Chair Jason Bogle stressed it remains a draft, and public-comment hearings before the Board of Commissioners were expected to begin around mid-November 2026, ahead of the statutory deadline. Commissioner Marc Sortman has repeatedly clarified that the county's own zoning authority covers only the 19 municipalities in its zoning partnership (which does not include Muncy Township, a separate PA MPC curative-amendment moratorium already tracked in this inventory as pa-muncy-township-2026); other municipalities must adopt their own ordinances.
